explanation: Explicit moral vocabulary: 'eliminate the divide' (equality), 'fair legal system' (fairness), and 'respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians' (rights/respect) — directly matching clarification (a).

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: 'Eliminate remaining inequality' uses equality/inequality vocabulary explicitly listed in the codebook, even though attached to tax policy.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Reports a legal obligation (0.7% GNI on aid enshrined in law); descriptive/legal framing without moral-evaluative language.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: Descriptive account of a private member's bill and 'problems faced by private tenants'; instrumental without moral vocabulary.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: Funding commitment for aged care beds; administrative.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Community policing structures described in partnership terms; instrumental governance language, no moral vocabulary.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Fiscal appeal (save money, cut waste); economic argument per negative clarification.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: Aspirational vision ('best place to grow up and grow old') lacking explicit moral vocabulary; 'best' is a generic positive adjective.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Administrative reform of ministerial car entitlements; no moral vocabulary.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: Borderline: the attack centres on opponents' untrustworthiness — a moral character/integrity judgment — compounded by alleged concealment of a danger (poisoned baby milk), framing a moral wrong; classified 1 as a vice/character evaluation rather than mere competence critique, though one could read it as a partisan credibility attack.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: Procedural mechanism (lottery for TDs' Bills); no moral content.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: 'Honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' invokes honor and patriotic commemoration of national figures — virtue/patriotism language per clarification (b).

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration framed by economic needs; instrumental per negative clarification.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: 'Right accountability framework' uses 'right' as 'appropriate', not as rights; governance/administrative language.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: 'Victory of free nations in the War on Terror' appeals to freedom as a value and frames terror as a moral enemy — freedom appeals are explicitly included in the codebook.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: Procedural rule on debate time; no moral content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: Enforcement/compliance appeal about poachers; law-and-order instrumental framing without explicit moral vocabulary.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: Jobs-created statistic; empirical achievement claim per negative example pattern.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: Aspiration for constitutional stability; neutral, no moral vocabulary.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: 'Dysfunctional' is a performance adjective, not moral vocabulary; administrative reform critique.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: Technical critique of waste strategy (scale, traffic, recycling conflicts); instrumental.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Aspirational economic transition language ('prosperous, decarbonized economy'); no moral vocabulary.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: Business competitiveness aspiration; economic framing.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: 'A fair share' of revenue should be returned — explicit fairness vocabulary and a normative claim listed in the codebook's definition and clarification (a).

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Sports participation and volunteering statistics; empirical.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognition of Maori enterprise's economic contribution; instrumental/descriptive without moral-evaluative vocabulary (weaker than 'honours'; about the economy).

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: Commitment to implement the Military Covenant; although the covenant carries moral connotations, the text itself is an instrumental implementation pledge without moral-evaluative language.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Critique that the funding cap 'acts against new and smaller parties'; a structural/political-competition argument without explicit moral vocabulary like unfair or discriminatory; borderline but framed instrumentally.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: Direct invocation of 'fairness' as a value Mr Howard has forgotten — explicit moral vocabulary under clarification (a) and a moral character critique.

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: Programme development commitment (PAFT); instrumental.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: Trade enforcement measure (anti-dumping crackdown); instrumental.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: Commitment to equip Defence Forces to meet international 'obligations'; descriptive of treaty/role commitments, instrumental rather than moral-duty rhetoric.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: Administrative critique of processing delays and litigation; no moral vocabulary.
